$comment: The visual language, in one place.
macOS renders in SwiftUI and the other platforms render in a web view, and
that difference is deliberate: only native code can call Apple's Liquid
Glass, which samples and refracts what is behind the window. CSS can blur;
it cannot lens. Forcing one renderer onto both would mean giving that up to
What is shared is the language, and it is shared as data rather than by
copying numbers between two files. scripts/generate-tokens.py writes both
sides from this, and check.sh fails if either has drifted.

radius.$comment: Concentric: a control inside a surface takes the smaller radius so the curves stay parallel.

space.$comment: One rhythm, so nothing is nudged by eye.

stroke.$comment: Opacity, not colour: the colour comes from the system's label so it follows light and dark on its own.

motion.$comment: Milliseconds. Reduced Motion turns these to zero rather than shortening them.
